summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis on chronic immunosuppression was admitted two days after an anal fistulotomy for right submandibular swelling, erythema, and pain. Initial evaluation revealed sialadenitis with imaging showing fluid and gas near the gland, raising concern for early Ludwig’s angina. He was started on clindamycin, warm compresses, sialogogues, and gland expression by ENT. A repeat CT showed worsening of the infected sialocele but no abscess or airway compromise. His symptoms improved over the next two days, white count trended down, and he became afebrile and tolerating oral intake. Thrush noted on admission improved with clotrimazole and was discontinued at discharge. He was discharged home on oral clindamycin to complete a 10-day course, with follow-up arranged with ENT and instructions to resume his baseline immunosuppressive regimen after antibiotics.
